title: BLS Average Price item to USDA FoodData Central nutrient map
purpose: Pipeline input for scripts/build_bls_timeseries.py. Each matched entry pairs one BLS Average Price food item with one USDA FoodData Central record and states, in full, how the BLS priced unit converts to grams of edible food. Skipped entries stay in this file on purpose: a public gap is an honest outcome, a forced match is not.

conventions.grams_per_priced_unit: Gross grams of product in the unit BLS prices, BEFORE any refuse is removed. For a per lb. (453.6 gm) item this is 453.6 by definition. For per doz. eggs and per gal. milk it is derived from the FDC record's own published portion weights, never from an outside constant.
conventions.edible_fraction: Share of grams_per_priced_unit that is edible food. 1.0 for boneless, peel-free, refuse-free items. Below 1.0 only where the USDA record itself publishes a yield or refuse figure that can be cited.
conventions.edible_grams_per_priced_unit: grams_per_priced_unit * edible_fraction. This is the quantity the per-dollar identity divides by. It is not stored here; the script derives it so the two documented inputs stay independently checkable.
conventions.convention_normalization_note: The upstream mapping pass recorded whole chicken (item 706111) as grams_per_priced_unit = 276 together with edible_fraction = 0.61, which would apply the same yield twice. This file normalizes that single row to the convention used by every other row and by the published flagship CSV public/data/protein-per-dollar-2026.csv: grams_per_priced_unit = 453.6 (the gross priced pound stated in the BLS unit string) and edible_fraction = 0.61 (the FDC record's own yield of 276.0 g meat and skin per 453.6 g ready-to-cook bird, 276.0 / 453.6 = 0.6085, published in the repo as 0.61). No value was invented: 453.6 comes from the BLS unit string, 0.61 comes from the FDC record and the existing repo CSV, and the product 453.6 * 0.61 = 276.7 g reproduces the record's 276.0 g yield to within 0.25 percent and reproduces the flagship row's published 25.3 g protein per dollar.
conventions.protein_and_fiber_basis: Grams per 100 g of edible food, as USDA publishes them.
conventions.value_precision: Where the repo already carried a full-precision SR Legacy value for the same FDC record, that value is used. Otherwise the value comes from https://fdc.nal.usda.gov/portal-data/external/{fdc_id}, which rounds to 3 significant figures. Every entry states which.

sources.prices: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, Average Price Data (AP), public API v2, keyless
sources.nutrients: USDA FoodData Central, SR Legacy unless stated otherwise
sources.bls_series_id_format: AP + U + 4-char area code + 6-char item code

coverage_note: This file carries 20 matched items across three food groups: meat-poultry-fish (12), dairy-eggs (5), grains-pantry-legumes (3). The upstream mapping payload delivered to the build agent was truncated part-way through the third grains item, so any further grains, legume, produce, or pantry mappings that were produced were never received and are absent here rather than guessed. See truncation_disclosure below.

truncation_disclosure.detail: The mapping payload was cut off mid-sentence inside the conversion_note for item 701322 (Spaghetti and macaroni). All six numeric fields for that item arrived intact and are recorded verbatim; only the tail of its prose note is missing, and the note is marked accordingly. Any matched or skipped items after 701322 in that group, and any additional groups (produce, pantry, legumes, fruit, vegetables), were never delivered. The curated item file pipeline-data/bls/ap.item.food.tsv lists 67 food items; 20 are mapped here and 15 are documented as skipped, leaving 32 items neither mapped nor adjudicated. Those 32 are NOT skipped-with-a-reason, they are unprocessed, and the distinction is preserved so nobody reads this file as a finished census.

matched.bls_item_name: Milk, fresh, whole, fortified, per gal. (3.8 lit)
matched.fdc_description: Milk, whole, 3.25% milkfat, with added vitamin D
matched.conversion_note: Volume to mass conversion taken from the FDC record's own portion weights rather than an outside density figure. FDC 171265 publishes quart = 976.0 g, so 1 US gallon = 4 quarts = 3904 g. Cross-checked independently against the same record's fl oz = 30.5 g, giving 128 fl oz = 3904 g. The two published portions agree exactly. Implied density is 3904 g / 3785.41 mL = 1.031 g/mL, consistent with published whole milk density, but no external density constant was needed. The BLS item name specifies fortified, which selects the with-added-vitamin-D record over FDC 172217 (without added vitamin A and vitamin D); both report identical 3.15 g protein, so the variant choice does not move the value.

skipped.bls_item_name: Ground chuck, 100% beef, per lb. (453.6 gm)
skipped.why: No USDA counterpart. A search of SR Legacy, Foundation Foods and FNDDS for ground chuck returns zero records: USDA publishes ground beef only by fat percentage (70/30 through 97/3) plus grass-fed, never by primal. Retail ground chuck is not a fixed composition, so choosing a fat level would be an invented conversion. Mapping it to FDC 174036 (80/20) would also duplicate the mapping already used for BLS 703112 without any independent evidence. This series is live and useful (114 monthly points, 2026-M06 at 6.975 per lb), so it is worth revisiting only if a defensible fat-level source appears.

skipped.bls_item_name: Chicken breast, bone-in, per lb. (453.6 gm)
skipped.why: Conversion cannot be documented. The nutrient match is clean (FDC 171474, Chicken, broilers or fryers, breast, meat and skin, raw, 20.8 g protein per 100 g), but the priced unit is bone-in and the record's totalRefuse field reads 0 on the portal-data endpoint, which does not publish USDA refuse. The record's own household measures do not help: 0.5 breast, bone removed = 145 g and 0.5 breast, bone removed (yield from 1 lb ready-to-cook chicken) = 87 g both describe yields from the whole bird, not the meat-and-skin share of a bone-in breast pack, so unlike whole chicken FDC 171447 there is no self-contained yield to divide by 453.6. Price: BLS series APU0000706211 also returns zero data points for 2017 through 2026.

skipped.bls_item_name: Chicken legs, bone-in, per lb. (453.6 gm)
skipped.why: Conversion cannot be documented, and this is the most painful skip in the group because the series is live and cheap (114 monthly points, 2026-M06 at 1.688 per lb). The nutrient match is clean (FDC 172378, Chicken, broilers or fryers, leg, meat and skin, raw, 16.4 g protein per 100 g) but the priced unit is bone-in and portal-data returns totalRefuse 0, publishing no refuse percentage. The record's measures (1 leg with skin = 344 g, drumstick with skin = 111 g, thigh with skin = 185 g, back with skin = 49 g) are part weights that do not state the bone share, so no edible fraction can be derived from the record itself. Reinstate this row only with a citable USDA refuse figure, matching the SR28 refuse citation the repo already uses for drumsticks FDC 172373. REVISIT PATH, recorded rather than acted on: this site already publishes a bone-in poultry row with a citable refuse figure, protein-per-dollar row 11, chicken drumsticks, edible_fraction 0.67 sourced as 'USDA SR28 refuse: 33% bone and cartilage' against FDC 172373. That precedent is NOT reused here because a whole leg is drumstick plus thigh and carries a different bone ratio than a drumstick alone, so the 33% figure is not transferable without a leg-specific refuse source. Resolve by reading the SR28 refuse value for the leg record itself, then this row can ship.

skipped.bls_item_name: Turkey, frozen, whole, per lb. (453.6 gm)
skipped.why: Conversion cannot be documented. FDC 171081, Turkey, whole, meat and skin, raw (21.6 g protein per 100 g) is the right food and the right form, but the priced unit is a bone-in ready-to-cook bird, portal-data returns totalRefuse 0, and the record's only measures are 1 bird = 5002 g and 4 oz = 113 g, neither of which states the yield per pound of ready-to-cook bird. skipped.bls_item_name: Tuna, light, chunk, per lb. (453.6 gm)
skipped.why: Drained-versus-net ambiguity that USDA's own data cannot settle, plus a dead series. USDA publishes canned light tuna only as drained solids (FDC 173709, 19.44 g protein per 100 g in the repo CSV), with no total-can-contents record for tuna of the kind that exists for pink salmon (FDC 173690). BLS prices canned goods on package net weight, which includes the packing water, so a drained fraction is required. The record's own measures conflict: 1 can = 165 g against 1 can (12.5 oz), drained = 315 g, which implies 88.9% of net weight, while current retail labels run nearer 80% (a 5 oz net can declaring 4 oz drained, the basis the repo used for its Walmart row). No defensible single factor, so the row is left out. Price: BLS series APU0000707111 returns only 8 points and ends at 2017-M09.

skipped.bls_item_name: Milk, fresh, low fat, per gal. (3.8 lit)
skipped.why: DISCONTINUED SERIES, the disqualifying reason. APU0000709213 returns zero data points from the BLS API for 2025-2026 and also zero for 2015-2024, so it has no current or recent history at the U.S. city average area and cannot participate in a self-refreshing dataset. Retired in the same 2018 BLS item-structure revision that started FJ4101 and FS1101, and unlike butter and yogurt it has no live successor in the curated item file. A secondary reason would have applied even if the series were live: BLS publishes no milkfat specification for 'low fat'. FDA labelling reserves lowfat milk for 1% milkfat and requires 2% to be sold as reduced fat, which points to FDC 746772 (Milk, lowfat, fluid, 1% milkfat, with added vitamin A and vitamin D, protein 3.38, cup = 246.0 g, hence 16 cups = 3936 g per gallon), but that record is Foundation Foods rather than SR Legacy, publishes no dietary fiber value, and the BLS series predates the 1998 labelling rule. Recording the groundwork here so the row can be added if BLS ever revives a low fat milk series.

skipped.bls_item_name: Butter, salted, grade AA, stick, per lb. (453.6 gm)
skipped.why: DISCONTINUED SERIES. APU0000710111 returns zero data points for 2025-2026 and zero for 2015-2024. Superseded by FJ-era item FS1101 (Butter, stick, per lb.), which begins 2018-M04 and is live through 2026-M06. The underlying food is NOT lost from the dataset: it is captured by the matched FS1101 row, mapped to FDC 173410. Including both codes would double-count the same butter price and would put a dead series into a dataset whose entire premise is monthly self-refresh.

skipped.bls_item_name: Yogurt, natural, fruit flavored, per 8 oz. (226.8 gm)
skipped.why: DISCONTINUED SERIES. APU0000710122 returns zero data points for 2025-2026 and zero for 2015-2024. Superseded by FJ4101 (Yogurt, per 8 oz.), which begins 2018-M04. The successor is itself skipped on match grounds, see the FJ4101 entry, so this food is genuinely absent from the dataset rather than relocated.

LIVE SERIES BUT NO DEFENSIBLE SINGLE USDA COUNTERPART, so it is left out rather than forced. The unit is unproblematic: per 8 oz. (226.8 gm) is a direct mass unit. The match is the problem. The BLS item name is bare 'Yogurt' with no fat level and no plain-versus-flavored specification, and USDA's yogurt records are stratified along BOTH axes, with protein per 100 g spanning roughly 3.5 to 9.5 across them: 171284 plain whole milk 3.47, 171304 Greek plain whole milk 9.00, 172208 chocolate nonfat 3.53, 172219 vanilla low fat 4.93. Worse, USDA subdivides fruit yogurt by protein content itself, 171285 'fruit, low fat, 10 grams protein per 8 ounce' at 4.37 versus 171286 'fruit, low fat, 11g protein/8 oz' at 4.86, so selecting a record would literally be selecting the answer this dataset is supposed to measure. Inheriting the retired 710122 'fruit flavored' wording would not rescue it, because BLS broadened the item definition when it renamed the series and the fat level is still unstated either way. No single record is defensible; a citable DOI package should not carry a coin flip.

unprocessed_items_note: The remaining items in pipeline-data/bls/ap.item.food.tsv (bread, cookies, crackers, fruit, vegetables, canned goods, sugar, peanut butter, potato chips, pork and beans, romaine lettuce, and the rest of the grains and legumes block) are neither matched nor skipped here. They were not adjudicated, because the upstream mapping payload was truncated before those groups were delivered. Do not read their absence as a judgement that no defensible match exists.
